linkTip: A hard link is a second name for the same file and takes no space. It only works when source and target are on the same disk or in the same pool.
clashTip: With Ask you decide for each file, otherwise your choice holds for all of them without asking.
keepAttrsTip: Owner, permissions and modification time stay as in the original. Without this switch new files belong to nobody:users (99:100).
verifyTip: Reads the target again after copying and compares the checksums.
background: Runs as a job in the background
forAllTip: Sets every row below to the same answer. Replace only newer replaces a file only when the new one was changed more recently, and skips it otherwise.

leftOut.one: 1 item stayed behind because it lies outside the folders here
leftOut.other: {n} items stayed behind because they lie outside the folders here

parityText: Unraid is checking parity right now. A copy of {size} slows the check down and runs slower itself.
parityWaits: The job waits until the parity check is done

space.title: This will not fit
space.noDisk: No disk of {share} has more than the minimum free space of {floor}. Unraid would not even start the copy.
space.tooMuch: Together it is {total}, but the disks of {share} only have {room} free above the minimum.
space.bigFile: Unraid would pick {disk}, because it has more than the minimum free space of {floor} (allocation {alloc}). The largest file, {name} with {size}, does not fit into the {free} free there. The copy would stop halfway.
space.poolFull: {pool} only has {free} free, and {total} is needed. Unraid would stop the copy halfway.
space.tip: Set the share's minimum free space to at least the largest file and Unraid skips disks that are too full by itself.

sameAlert: Source and target are the same file
sameText: {disk} is a disk share, {user} the user share above it. Both point at the same files. {verb} from one to the other cuts them to 0 bytes, and the data is gone.
wayTip: It is safe when both sides are disk shares or both are user shares. Only mixing them is dangerous.
targetDiskTip: What lies on {disk} goes onto this disk. In the user share it stays visible in the same place.
planNothing: Through the user shares source and target are the same folder. The files are there already, there is nothing to do.
linksCopy: The copy is not a hard link
linksCopyText: A copy is a new file and takes {size} once more. The other paths stay linked to the original.
linksMoveText: Going to {dest} crosses a share or pool border, which makes a new file. The other paths keep their data, and afterwards {size} lie there twice.
linksNo: A hard link does not work here, because the target is on another disk or in another pool.

linked.one: 1 hard link made, taking no new space
linked.other: {n} hard links made, taking no new space

noLink: A hard link only works on the same disk or in the same pool
sameSkipTip: The target holds the same file under another path, for example as a hard link or through a disk share and the user share. It stays as it is.

sameSkipped.one: {n} file skipped because it is the same file at the target
sameSkipped.other: {n} files skipped because they are the same files at the target

nothingCopied.one: Nothing copied. The file at the target is the same one and stays as it is
nothingCopied.other: Nothing copied. The {n} files at the target are the same ones and stay as they are

nothingMoved.one: Nothing moved. The file at the target is the same one and stays as it is
nothingMoved.other: Nothing moved. The {n} files at the target are the same ones and stay as they are
